Q1.problem_type_and_essence: precedence-constrained DAG list scheduling minimizing peak live-buffer residency

input_target_constraints.input: DAG nodes/edges with ALLOC/FREE/compute operations and buffer sizes

baseline.name: Kahn ready-set + FREE-first + critical-path/slack urgency + incremental-memory tie-break
six_hour_plan: schedule legal FREE immediately; among remaining ready nodes prioritize path urgency before allocation-size tie-break
replay Vstay and compare all six workloads
baseline.why: deterministic, transparent, cheap and the case-group mini transfer test exposed that tie-break ordering materially matters

author_route.method: three greedy policies (MinPeak/EarlyFree/LateAlloc) plus SA/TS/GA comparison; EarlyFree chosen as final contest route
why_fit: greedy scales to very large DAGs
paper explicitly weighs runtime/reproducibility against heuristic improvement
SA/TS/GA can reveal graph-dependent remaining search room
author_route.evidence_boundary: printed greedy/TS excerpts are visible but SA/GA full executable chain is incomplete; LateAlloc/MinPeak allocation-size priority direction in code conflicts with prose intuition.

major_alternatives.why_can_work: benefits flexible ready sets such as FlashAttention/Conv
major_alternatives.when_prefer: only after matched-budget gain over deterministic baseline

major_alternatives.why_can_work: keeps several promising legal partial schedules without population overhead
major_alternatives.when_prefer: medium graphs with measurable baseline exact-gap

not_recommended.model: full GA as default contest mainline
not_recommended.why_not_now: high evaluation budget and no stable cross-seed advantage shown over EarlyFree
no graph-instance training distribution or evidence that training amortizes within contest time

switch_conditions: keep simple greedy if metaheuristic improvement is small/unstable
refine only graph families with large ready-set flexibility and measured gap

Q2.problem_type_and_essence: lifetime-aware cache address allocation plus SPILL victim/rule selection minimizing extra transfer while preserving feasibility

input_target_constraints.objective: minimize extra transfer; any secondary peak/time objective must be explicitly normalized or constrained

baseline.name: lifetime sweep + coalescing free-list + Best-Fit/linear-scan + deficit-aware minimum incremental-transfer spill subset
six_hour_plan: derive lifetimes and maintain free intervals
on overflow compute legal victims and the minimum transfer cost set sufficient to free the deficit
replay capacity/non-overlap/transfer bytes from one registry
baseline.why: directly optimizes the byte contract and remains inspectable; mini transfer shows one-by-one cheapest-victim can be suboptimal when one victim does not free enough space

author_route.method: GP evolves spill rules / chooses allocator family; VN-SA for normalized peak-transfer tradeoff
why_fit: rule search can adapt to heterogeneous graph/cache patterns
GP can yield interpretable heuristic expressions
VNS+SA can perturb a fixed schedule when allocation and peak conflict
author_route.evidence_boundary: Table14→Table16 FlashAttention1 provenance is unresolved; Eq4-10 optimizes Peak+transfer but later algorithm text switches to time+transfer; printed VN-SA defining loop is incomplete.

major_alternatives.why_can_work: lifetimes naturally form intervals and it is deterministic
can learn rule combinations beyond first/best/worst fit
major_alternatives.when_prefer: only with enough independent training graphs and held-out validation
small buffer sets or time windows

not_recommended.why_not_now: separate tuning on only a few fixed graph structures is not independent transfer evidence

not_recommended.model: Min-Max weighted sum with moving observed extrema
not_recommended.why_not_now: normalization range changes objective semantics across runs and can hide a hard engineering priority

switch_conditions: promote GP only if held-out graph-family performance beats deterministic baseline
resolve one canonical objective (Peak vs Time as secondary) before search
never rank Table16 result whose Table14 provenance cannot be replayed

Q3.problem_type_and_essence: reduce execution time while controlling extra transfer; optionally characterize feasible cycle-transfer tradeoff

input_target_constraints.input: Q2 feasible baseline + scheduler/cache execution model
input_target_constraints.objective: minimize cycles under canonical transfer cap; Pareto frontier optional
hard_constraints: canonical transfer cap from original problem statement

baseline.name: epsilon-constraint search: enforce canonical Q2 transfer cap first, then minimize execution cycles
six_hour_plan: read canonical epsilon from original task contract
reference Q2 baseline by Result Registry run_id, never hand-copy
apply local resource-aware schedule/allocation moves and select minimum-cycle feasible solution
baseline.why: hard constraints have priority over arbitrary weighted sums and give a clear deployable operating point

author_route.method: stage-1 GP weighted objective, then NSGA-II (paper often says NAGA-II) + MOPSO Pareto search
why_fit: Pareto search is suitable if multiple feasible tradeoff points are genuinely required
dual optimizers can provide robustness comparison
paper uses convergence/frontier figures rather than only one number
author_route.evidence_boundary: 10% cap conflicts with S025 5% contract; Table20/Table21 contain baseline, lexicographic-selection and FlashAttention0 time-scale inconsistencies; loaded GP tree is regenerated randomly rather than reconstructed from spill_operations in printed code.

major_alternatives.why_can_work: directly respects transfer cap with lower overhead
useful when decision maker needs full verified frontier
major_alternatives.when_prefer: only after common evaluator and correct operating-point selection

major_alternatives.why_can_work: validates cap and time model on reduced instances

not_recommended.model: raw weighted sum without canonical normalization
not_recommended.why_not_now: weights depend on unit/range and can trade away a hard cap

not_recommended.model: two metaheuristics compared by self-reported table values only
not_recommended.why_not_now: selection rule and baselines must first be internally consistent

switch_conditions: resolve 5% vs 10% from original problem statement before optimization
use Pareto only if multiple operating points are needed and frontier passes feasibility replay
if heuristic does not beat epsilon baseline materially under matched budget, keep it out of mainline
